originalPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE game background atlas, arranged as four equal panels in a strict 2 by 2 grid, edge to edge, no gutters, no borders. Wide whole-image aspect ratio 8:5 (ideally 1600 by 1000). Each panel is a complete landscape scene with the same 8:5 aspect ratio.
Primary request: Rich, polished pixel art backgrounds for a gentle mystery space adventure for a young reader, on a Game Boy Color style handheld. Professional late-1990s handheld pixel art with deliberate pixel clusters, clean silhouettes, carefully placed highlights, textured rocks and foliage, rich navy, teal, mint, violet and warm amber palette. It must still read when each panel is displayed at 160 by 100 pixels. No text, symbols, letters, numbers, UI, borders or labels anywhere.
The spacecraft must remain exactly recognizable across panels: small rounded pearl-silver alien craft with a wide dark-teal canopy, jade/mint fins, twin compact engine pods, brass details, luminous turquoise seams and a little antenna. Affectionate adventurous tone, no threat, no alien visible in any scene.
TOP LEFT PANEL: NIGHT BACKYARD DISCOVERY. A cozy house at left with one warmly lit window, wooden fence, layered trees and distant hills, deep violet starry sky with small Moon. The damaged ship rests tilted at center-right in a shallow furrow, one folded bent fin, dark cockpit glass and a small glow at its hatch. Scattered leaves and tufts of grass. A single fallen mint crystal rests in front of the ship. A very small child explorer with a dark brown bob, mustard jacket, dark trousers and tiny backpack stands at lower-left looking toward it. Ship and child are large enough to read as silhouettes. No flames, no smoke.
TOP RIGHT PANEL: SAME NIGHT BACKYARD AFTER REPAIR. Keep the house, fence, trees, camera angle and positions nearly identical. The same child stands admiring the same craft now level on little landing feet, both jade fins unfolding symmetrically, a clear canopy, beautiful lit turquoise hull seams, soft pools of light in the grass. Crystal now fitted into the hull. Ship is visibly more detailed and inviting.
BOTTOM LEFT PANEL: EMPTY COCKPIT. View from the open entry toward ONE visibly empty rounded pilot seat, semicircular dashboard, little physical switches, blank luminous mint monitors, small amber status lights, curved structural ribs, neat cables, patterned floor plates, broad forward window showing stars and a small distant Moon. Preserve the same silver/teal design language. No person, no alien, no hologram figure, no text or glyphs on monitors.
BOTTOM RIGHT PANEL: MOON ARRIVAL. The same restored craft rests left-of-center on textured blue-gray lunar ground, landing feet extended, both mint fins and luminous seams visible. One small child in a cream space suit with dark teal visor stands near the ship. Craters, small angular stones and layered jagged horizon under black/navy starry sky, tiny distant blue Earth. On the right, a small golden signal lamp stands beyond a shallow crater and emits a gentle glow. No alien or other beings. No giant planets.
Composition constraints: each exact quadrant is a distinct full-bleed illustration. Keep key subjects away from panel edges. Artwork only, no text. Use well-separated simple planes and sophisticated pixel shading. No painterly blur, no anti-aliased vector look, no photographic texture, no thick gridlines, no platform/controller mockup.
revisionPrompt: Edit only the scenery seen through the windows in the BOTTOM LEFT quadrant of this four-panel pixel-art atlas. This empty cockpit is still parked in a backyard on EARTH before launch. Replace the barren lunar-looking horizon seen through all three cockpit windows with a dark wooded Earth backyard horizon: silhouettes of leafy trees, a few shrubs, a wooden fence and distant forested hills beneath the existing starry sky and small crescent Moon. Keep the cockpit interior, seat, dashboard, materials, framing, monitor lights and every pixel outside those windows unchanged. Preserve the other THREE quadrants exactly, including the lunar ground in the BOTTOM RIGHT. Preserve image size, exact 2 by 2 grid, pixel art style, and no text. No additional beings or characters.
note: Artwork generated as a four-panel concept atlas, then revised to keep the cockpit on Earth before launch. The prompt record omits the original player name. WebP is a format conversion for embedding. The game tools convert the PNG into cartridge palettes and tiles.
